sections.skill: Tell training from inference (using the model)

questions.prompt: A company shows a model millions of labeled photos and adjusts it until it sorts them well. Which stage is this?

choices.text: Inference, because the model is being used on photos
Inference, because the photos are labeled
Neither, because sorting photos is not AI
Training

questions.correct_answer: Training
questions.intro: An AI model has two very different stages. TRAINING is when the model learns: it is shown large amounts of example data and its internal settings are adjusted again and again until its outputs match the examples well. Training happens before you use the model and usually takes a lot of computing power. INFERENCE (or simply "using the model") is when the finished model takes NEW input, such as your question or photo, and produces an output. During ordinary use the model's learned settings do not change. Typing a question into an app is inference, not training.
questions.feedback: Adjusting the model to match examples is training.

sections.skill: Compare studying for a driving test with driving

questions.prompt: Practicing with a driving teacher is like which stage?

choices.text: Inference
Neither stage
Both stages equally
Training

questions.correct_answer: Training
questions.intro: Think about learning to drive. While you STUDY and PRACTICE with a teacher, you make mistakes, get corrected and slowly improve: that is like TRAINING. Once you have your license and drive to a store, you use what you learned on a new road. You are not taking lessons on that trip: that is like INFERENCE. An AI model is similar. It learns during training, which happens first and takes a long time. Later it uses what it learned on new input, quickly, without changing what it learned.
questions.feedback: Practice and correction are training.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Ask what actually changes when a product seems to "learn"

questions.prompt: You click "thumbs down" on a wrong answer. What is the most accurate description?

choices.text: It instantly retrains the model to fix that answer for everyone
It deletes the model and replaces it with a better one at once
It is feedback the company may use later, depending on its policy
It has no possible use for anyone at all

questions.correct_answer: It is feedback the company may use later, depending on its policy
questions.intro: Products can blur the line between training and use, so it helps to ask exactly what changes. Rating an answer "thumbs up" or "thumbs down" does not instantly retrain the model; a company MAY later use such feedback, along with other data, to train a new version, depending on its policies. Some products keep notes about you between conversations, which feels like learning but is stored information the product feeds back in, not a change to the model's settings. When you want to know whether your data could be used for training, read the provider's data policy and settings.
questions.feedback: Feedback may inform later training, depending on policy.
